ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against UN Consolidated List, UK/Gibraltar Sanctions List and OFAC SDN list; enhanced due diligence for all PEPs, their family members and close associates; senior management approval required for high-risk and PEP relationships; re-screening at least every 90 days; ongoing transaction monitoring and source-of-funds verification for the e-commerce payment rails (Stripe and Affirm BNPL).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies House Gibraltar (Companies Registry) - official Government of Gibraltar portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Roman/Latin alphabet; English is the working language; no transliteration into local script is required. Non-Latin or foreign script names must be accompanied by a certified English translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is renewable for one further 30-day period at the Registrar's discretion. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may resubmit a revised name within 14 days; an administrative review may be requested from the Registrar within 21 days; further appeal lies to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar under the Companies Act 2014. No extra search fee is charged on resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for registered-office purposes through a licensed corporate services provider, provided a valid physical service-of-process address is maintained in Gibraltar. However, for the target online retail business, banks and Gibraltar EMIs will require demonstrable commercial substance (e.g., local director/employee or serviced office) to open merchant and corporate accounts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% for non-licensed retail e-commerce; probability rises materially if the UBO/beneficial owner is a PEP, if sanctions hits occur, or if the company fails the economic substance initial screen.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 132), as amended, ss. 10-12 (incorporation by registration), s. 20 (name restrictions), s. 31 (memorandum and articles), and ss. 108-116 (first directors and company secretary); read with the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar) provisions governing non-resident exempt-company status.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, a directorate of the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, H.M. Government of Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Private Company, comprising the Memorandum and Articles of Association, Statement of Compliance, and subscriber share statements, delivered to the Registrar of Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 for an exempted private company limited by shares; a single subscriber share may be issued at nominal value. No escrow or blocked deposit account is mandated by Gibraltar law, although a licensed corporate services provider may require paid-up share premiums to be held in a client account pending bank onboarding.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED as the first resolution of the board: (1) the share subscriptions set out in the register of members are accepted and the first and further allotments of shares are approved in accordance with the Articles of Association; (2) the registered office of the Company is fixed at the principal office of its licensed corporate services provider and the Companies Registry is directed to record that address; (3) the persons named in the register of directors and the register of secretaries are appointed as the first directors and company secretary; (4) the directors are authorized to execute all statutory returns, open banking and payment-rail accounts, and engage professional advisers; and (5) this resolution takes effect as of the date of the certificate of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry via a GFSC-licensed corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the reserved-name application through the licensed company manager's e-filing credentials, stating the proposed corporate name and the principal business of direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels (ISIC 4791). The Registrar checks the name against the restrictions in s. 20 of the Companies Act 2014 and issues a name reservation.
required_dossiers: Reserved-name application form
AML/KYC file of each subscriber and ultimate beneficial owner (passport, proof of address, source of funds)
Letter of engagement with the GFSC-licensed corporate services provider
Principal business description (online retail of solar portable power equipment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as prohibited, offensive, or confusingly similar, the provider re-files a substitute name without additional state cost or submits the written consent of the prior rights-holder where similarity is not statutorily barred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and subscribers; Gibraltar notary public or licensed company manager with notarization authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and settle the Memorandum and Articles of Association, including the exempt-status declaration, limited-liability clause, share allotment authority, and board powers. Each subscriber executes the memorandum in counterparts, and the notary verifies subscriber signatures and the Statement of Compliance for filing with the Registry.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Signed subscriber statements under s. 31 of the Companies Act 2014
Consents to act as first directors and company secretary
Consent of the registered-office provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any Registry-flagged drafting deficiencies by executing supplemental articles or amended subscriber statements; re-notarization is confined to the affected signature pages and no new fee is incurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry, Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation bundle (memorandum, articles, Statement of Compliance, subscriber statements, and officer consents) through the Registry's online or counter submission procedure and pay the prescribed incorporation fee. The licensed company manager certifies the application for the private limited-company track.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Incorporation of a Private Company
Signed Statement of Compliance
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Evidence of payment of the state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a registry query or rejection, respond with corrected documents within the statutory 21-day query window; if the window is missed, file a fresh application with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Company Number Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the unique company number and records the registered office, first directors, and secretary on the public index. Obtain the certified extract and the physical certificate for the company's statutory minute book.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation application file
Company number reference allocated by the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical or surname errors, apply to the Registrar for administrative rectification; corrected certificates are re-issued without charge where the error is attributable to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Adoption of Statutory Registers, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First board of directors; company secretary; Gibraltar-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to approve the pro-forma board resolution, allot subscriber shares, fix the registered office, appoint the company secretary, open statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges, and PSC register), and file the notice of appointment of directors and registered office address with the Registry.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution
Register of members, register of directors, register of secretaries, and PSC register
Notice of registered office address
Beneficial-ownership declaration for the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defective or late officer notices are cured by filing amended notices with the Registry together with any late-filing penalty; statutory books are corrected by board resolution and re-signed entries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Non-Resident Exempt-Status Application and Tax-Exempt Zone Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office, H.M. Government of Gibraltar, acting through the licensed tax agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Commissioner of Income Tax for written confirmation that the Company is non-resident for tax purposes and therefore outside the scope of Gibraltar corporation tax on its non-Gibraltar source income. File the exempt-status declaration with the certificate of incorporation, UBO declarations, and evidence that management and control are exercised outside Gibraltar.
required_dossiers: Exempt-status application and non-residence declaration
Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents
UBO and director declarations confirming foreign management and control
Projected revenue model and source documentation for online retail sales
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office queries the management-and-control evidence, submit supplementary board minutes, meeting calendars, and service contracts demonstrating foreign control; an administrative review is available within 30 days of the query.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), H.M. Government of Gibraltar, in conjunction with the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service for battery-storage premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: WEEE Producer Registration Certificate and Portable Batteries (Placing on the Market) Registration under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013 (as retained and applied), together with a warehouse storage clearance for portable solar and battery goods.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), H.M. Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration category (Category C): no Full EIA Report is triggered for a non-manufacturing, direct online retail operation; only environmental registration, waste compliance, and producer-obligation filings are required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero process wastewater and no VOC emissions from retail-only activity; Waste Duty-of-Care consignment notes for battery and e-waste disposal; compliance with WEEE recovery and recycling targets for solar panels and portable power equipment; lithium-cell storage held below the hazardous-waste registration threshold (5 tonnes) at ambient temperature; packaging waste registration required if packaging handled exceeds 50 tonnes per annum.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service covering the registered office, warehouse, and lithium-battery charging or storage areas, including rated fire suppression and smoke detection; structural load certificate from a registered engineer for mezzanine or racked storage; and workplace clearance under the Employment (Safety, Health and Welfare) Act 1989 (Gibraltar) covering electrical safety, battery handling, and first-aid provision.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office of Gibraltar (HM Government of Gibraltar), official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation; HM Customs Gibraltar for indirect tax and customs clearances.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Bermuda Exempted Company must first register as an external company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under Part XXII of the Companies Act 2014. After obtaining the external registration number, it must file the prescribed non-resident tax registration form with the Income Tax Office, attaching the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of good standing, memorandum and articles, evidence of registered office in Bermuda, and particulars of any Gibraltar registered office and tax representative. The Income Tax Office issues a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (GIN). If the entity imports or holds dutiable goods in Gibraltar, it must additionally register with HM Customs Gibraltar for a Customs Identification Number; Gibraltar is outside the UK VAT area, so no UK VAT registration arises merely from Gibraltar incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Bermuda Exempted Company): The entity is a separate legal corporation, not a pass-through entity. Bermuda does not tax exempted companies. For Gibraltar tax purposes, absent central management and control in Gibraltar and absent a Gibraltar permanent establishment, the entity is non-resident and remains outside Gibraltar's corporation tax net. All offshore e-commerce sales income is therefore untaxed. If a taxable permanent establishment were created in Gibraltar, Gibraltar Income Tax at the flat corporate rate of 12.5% would apply to Gibraltar-source profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not maintain a check-the-box entity classification election. A foreign corporation cannot elect to be treated as a disregarded or transparent entity. Gibraltar's hybrid mismatch rules, implementing OECD BEPS Action 2 via the Income Tax (Hybrid and Other Mismatches) Regulations 2019, allow elective adjustments in respect of hybrid financial instruments and reverse-hybrid entities, including a dual-inclusion income offset election. Such elections affect the quantum or timing of relief but do not alter the entity's fundamental tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar Purchase Tax — a sales and use tax regime distinct from UK VAT; UK VAT may separately apply to distance sales into the United Kingdom if the entity is UK VAT-registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gibraltar Purchase Tax: no turnover registration threshold; Purchase Tax and customs duties are triggered at importation, and any importer, including a non-resident e-commerce seller using a Gibraltar warehouse, must obtain a Customs Identification Number. UK VAT: an overseas seller must register for UK VAT when UK taxable distance sales exceed GBP 90,000 in a rolling 12-month period (post-1 April 2024 threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar: no real-time fiscal clearance mandate, no electronic stamping, and no statutory e-invoicing requirement. Importers submit declarations via the Gibraltar Electronic Customs System using SAD or ENS filings. If the entity registers for UK VAT, it must file VAT returns through HMRC Making Tax Digital-compatible software; HMRC does not mandate real-time e-invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: To claim 0% VAT on exports from the UK, the exporter must be a UK VAT-registered taxable person; the goods must be exported to a non-UK destination, with export evidence obtained within 3 months and retained for 6 years; the sale must be to an overseas customer and the goods must not return to the UK. Directly connected delivery services may also be zero-rated. For Gibraltar Purchase Tax, goods exported from Gibraltar are outside the Purchase Tax charge, and Purchase Tax paid on importation may be refunded if the exporter proves physical exportation within the prescribed customs window and that the goods were not consumed or sold locally.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent export zero-rating claims are treated as deliberate inaccuracy, triggering penalty assessments up to 100% of the tax evaded, interest, and criminal prosecution. Under UK VAT, VATA 1994 Section 72 provides imprisonment up to 7 years and unlimited fines; HMRC may assess retrospectively for up to 4 years, extended to 20 years for fraud or concealment. In Gibraltar, HM Customs may claw back Purchase Tax refunded, impose civil penalties and penal assessments, seize goods, and prosecute false declaration offences under the Customs and Excise Duties Ordinance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England as monetary anchor for GBP and GIP; HM Government of Gibraltar Ministry of Finance as currency-issuing authority for the Gibraltar pound; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission as prudential and AML/CFT regulator for licensed banks and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar is a free-convertibility offshore special territory. Current-account receipts and capital-account transfers are freely convertible between GIP/GBP, USD and EUR without exchange-control approval. Profit remittances by a non-resident Bermuda exempted company through a Gibraltar treasury account are unrestricted in law, subject only to financial sanctions, AML/CFT documentation, correspondent-bank policy and the final-UBO assessment by the receiving bank. There is no dual exchange-rate mechanism and no requirement to convert foreign-currency receipts into local currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender period and no mandatory conversion ratio apply under United Kingdom or Gibraltar exchange-control rules. Export and online sales proceeds may be retained indefinitely in the original currency and may be applied directly to supplier settlements or converted at market rates. No 30, 60 or 90-day surrender timeline is imposed; statistical reporting may be required but does not restrict treasury management.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account - GBP and SWIFT/correspondent settlement
Operational Account and Trade Finance / Commercial LC facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-high as a secondary treasury rail for FX clearing, supplier disbursements and marketplace payouts, but low as the sole concentration bank. Legal constraints: (i) any EMI must be authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority in the UK or the GFSC in Gibraltar under the applicable electronic-money and payment-services framework; (ii) unlicensed offshore EMIs may not lawfully provide payment or e-money services to a Gibraltar-connect treasury function; (iii) funds held with an EMI are not covered by a statutory deposit-protection scheme; (iv) the EMI's distance-onboarding process will still require certified UBO data, payment-volume history and AML source-of-funds evidence; (v) capital escrow and tax reserves should remain with a fully licensed bank rather than an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for every director to appear physically at a Gibraltar bank, but most tier-1 banks will condition onboarding of an offshore Bermuda exempted company on either physical attendance of at least one director/UBO or verification by a Gibraltar-licensed corporate service provider or regulated introducer. Remote opening is permissible in principle through video identity verification, live financial-crime interview and digital source-of-funds evidence, but the bank will usually require a face-to-face or introducer meeting before granting multi-currency FX, trade-finance and high-limit operational facilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore Bermuda-incorporated exempted company with no formal audited financial statements, no physical commercial premises and nominee-director indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, Certificate of Good Standing from the Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Register of Directors and Members, current economic-substance filing status, Gibraltar corporate-service-provider engagement letter, desk/business-premises agreement, staffing and substance schedule, projected cashflows, and a board resolution specifically approving opening of the Gibraltar treasury account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity e-commerce settlements from Stripe and Affirm BNPL creating multiple small-denomination incoming transfers, frequent refunds and chargebacks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-processor merchant agreements, 90-day settlement reports, Stripe payout ledger, Affirm BNPL settlement reconciliation, refund/chargeback policy, transaction-level export prepared in the bank's requested format, website sales evidence and an explanatory memorandum on expected peak volumes, payout cycles and supplier counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure arising from shipment and freight payment corridors used for portable solar panels and battery generators, including high-risk transshipment jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screening logs, supplier KYB/KYC file, export declarations, Incoterms and bills of lading, no-transshipment undertakings, final-consignee declarations, HS commodity classification, freight-forwarder compliance attestations and trade credit insurance certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership through the Bermuda exempted company chain or non-face-to-face identity posture.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate structure chart through to natural persons, certified passports and proof of address for directors and UBOs, source-of-wealth report for the injected capital, negative-media and PEP/sanctions checks, signed PEP and adverse-media declarations, and a certification letter from a Gibraltar-licensed legal or corporate-services professional.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from the Bermuda parent or ultimate beneficial owners must be delivered through a fully licensed Gibraltar settlement bank. The compliant protocol is SWIFT MT103 for direct customer-to-bank credit and MT202 for interbank cover; the remittance field must state 'Equity capital contribution - non-refundable working capital - no trade invoice', and the structured purpose code must reflect 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' or the bank's equivalent 'EQUITY/CAPIT' code. The receiving bank must verify that the beneficiary IBAN and legal entity name exactly match the operational account opening documents. The documentary support pack includes a board resolution approving the capital injection, shareholder subscription/allotment minutes, source-of-funds declarations, the prior capital account ledger of the Bermuda entity, and an accounting treatment note.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements should be executed through SWIFT MT103 cover payments with full invoice references in field 70; European suppliers should be paid by SEPA Credit Transfer using ISO 20022 structured remittance information. Large purchases of solar panels and portable power equipment from Asia should be made under irrevocable documentary commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and amended through MT707, conforming to UCP600. Daily e-commerce payouts to marketplaces, Stripe and Affirm BNPL partners should be processed through bank bulk files over SWIFT gpi with automatic OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening and same-day USD/EUR sweeps. Dividends or management recharges back to the Bermuda parent should use SWIFT MT103 with a remittance text referencing the board dividend resolution and underlying accounts; no outbound payment may be made to sanctioned or high-risk blocked counterparties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in GIP/GBP, USD and EUR for committed trade settlement and e-commerce cash-flow cycles
FX swaps for short-term liquidity conversion between settlement currencies and the operational treasury base currency
Non-deliverable forwards on currencies subject to offshore convertibility restrictions, such as CNY, INR, BRL and IDR, cash-settled in USD against documented supplier exposures
Cross-currency swaps to align USD-denominated Stripe and BNPL settlement flows with GBP/EUR operating liabilities, used only as cash-flow hedges under an approved board treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation; annual fee cycle aligned to 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of BMD 500; continued default may result in administrative strike-off and forfeiture of Bermudian assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Economic Substance Authority / Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic penalty of BMD 10,000 for late filing, ongoing daily penalties, and possible revocation of economic substance/tax-exempt status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return for Overseas Company / External Registration Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of Gibraltar registration or regularisation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GIP 100, escalating daily fines up to GIP 5,000; persistent non-compliance may trigger strike-off of the Gibraltarian registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 13 months after the balance sheet date of the Bermuda foreign company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil penalty for late delivery, court-ordered filing, and potential strike-off of the Gibraltar branch registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Corporation Tax Annual Return / nil return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 11 months after the accounting period end; for a calendar year period, due by 30 November
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty not exceeding GIP 10,000, interest on any unpaid tax, estimated assessments by the Commissioner, and strike-off for continued default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Bermuda: statutory audit is mandatory for listed, licensed, or regulated exempted companies; a private exempted company may be exempt if its gross assets are below BMD 10 million and shareholders representing less than 10% of shares do not require an audit. Gibraltar: audit is mandatory if the company cannot meet the small-company exemption (turnover not exceeding GBP 6.5 million, balance sheet not exceeding GBP 3.26 million, employees not exceeding 50) or if regulated, listed, or parent-company audited accounts are required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is the primary framework for statutory financial statements; Bermuda GAAP or Gibraltar GAAP (FRS 102) may be applied by unregulated, non-listed exempt companies where the home Companies Act permits.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent or company secretary conducts an annual confirmation review covering the Register of Members, Register of Directors, and beneficial ownership records. Share transfers effected during the year must be recorded in the Bermuda Register of Members on execution and reflected in the annual return. For Gibraltar branch or registered status, beneficial ownership changes are notified to the Gibraltar Registry within 14 days, and the annual return confirms the UBO register remains accurate. Bermuda does not maintain a public UBO register, but the private UBO/AML register must be kept at the registered office and updated continuously.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: UBO / AML register held by the registered agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 2,800 for Bermuda registered office and corporate agent; plus USD 900 - USD 1,800 for Gibraltar branch agent coordination
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 9,500 for a full statutory audit if the audit exemption is unavailable; USD 1,500 - USD 3,000 for an independent review or compilation if exempt.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat rate on chargeable profits applicable to Gibraltar-resident companies and to non-resident companies trading through a Gibraltar permanent establishment (Gibraltar Income Tax Act, effective for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 April 2015).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions apply to e-commerce retail. The 'top-up' tax mechanism requires corporate tax to be not less than 10% of adjusted gross income, producing an effective tax rate between 10% and 12.5% depending on profit margins. Gibraltar levies no VAT, no capital gains tax (except gains on Gibraltar land), and permits indefinite carry-forward of trading losses, subject to continuity of trade and ownership. Rental and certain non-trading investment income may be subject to a separate higher statutory charge.
